about:
Local 92 – Mediterranean-Italian Dining & Cocktails in Soho

A Soho favorite blending Mediterranean flavor with Italian comfort. Led by Chef Shay Zivaback, Local 92 serves refined yet approachable dishes like the signature Chicken Regime and Mediterranean Tapas Platter, made with fresh herbs, grilled meats, and seasonal produce.

Mixologist David Asante crafts house-infused cocktails using botanicals that echo the menu’s coastal spirit. The brick-lined interior, warm lighting, and hidden backyard patio create a relaxed but elevated atmosphere perfect for dates or small groups.

Just steps from Washington Square Park and NYU, Local 92 offers soulful food, crafted cocktails, and a neighborhood energy that captures the best of Soho dining.

"If you want to casually impress someone with your exceptionally good taste in restaurants, take them to Loring Place." - Infatuation.

Loring Place by Award Winning Chef Dan Kluger, located just a block from Washington Square Park in New York’s Greenwich Village, offers the perfect NYC dining experience. Chef Kluger, known for his work at Union Square Café, Tabla, and ABC Kitchen, creates innovative, market-driven dishes with fresh ingredients from the Union Square Greenmarket featuring shareable small and large plates with unexpected, yet perfectly balanced flavor combinations.

Whether for an intimate dinner, a fun night out, or drinks at the bar, Loring Place provides the perfect downtown atmosphere and also offers two private rooms for events, accommodating groups of any size—ideal for corporate dinners, weddings, birthdays, graduations, media dinners and more.

Experience unforgettable cuisine and exceptional service at Loring Place, a top destination in Greenwich Village.

name: Lounge On Pearl
about:
Step into a hidden gem nestled in the heart of Lower Manhattan, our all-day lounge and bar beckons with a unique blend of comfort and sophistication. Immerse yourself in a space where modern aesthetics harmonize with vintage accents and opulent jewel tones beneath lofty ceilings. Whether you seek a productive workspace or a leisurely escape, this expansive lounge promises a chic haven away from the urban hustle.

Lounge on Pearl offers a curated selection of La Marchande's signature dishes under the guidance of Chef John Fraser. The menu showcases a lighter take on French cuisine, featuring delectable creations such as Mushroom Spring Rolls, Salted Cod & Scallop Fritters, and the indulgent Two Layer Club sandwich.

Helmed by Beverage Director Amy Racine, Lounge on Pearl boasts a martini-centric bar experience, from the timeless Not So Dirty Martini to the exotic French Martini.

about:
Lucky Tiger – Cocktail Bar, Asian Inspired, NY Bred
Lucky Tiger brings bold flavor, playful energy, and unforgettable hospitality to the heart of FiDi. This Asian-inspired, New York bred cocktail bar and restaurant serves creative cocktails and full dinner service in a vibrant, late-night setting with live DJ nights.

Our drinks mix innovation and comfort with clarified juices, rich textures, and unexpected twists that make every sip memorable. Signature favorites include the Lucky Tiger Sour and the viral Shrimp Cocktail. The menu features inventive dishes and full entrees designed to pair perfectly with our cocktails.

With four immersive spaces — Dragon Bar, Night Market, Bamboo Grove, and Toraya — Lucky Tiger is perfect for date nights, dinner parties, and late-night adventures. Come for the cocktails, stay for the energy.

faqs.question: FAQs
faqs.answer:
Is this a good pick for date night?

Yes, Lucky Tiger is a great spot for a date night if you enjoy lively, cocktail-forward evenings with shared plates. The space is an Asian-inspired cocktail bar with vibrant decor and a warm, energetic atmosphere that guests praise. Plan for drinks at the bar or a cozy table with small plates to share (bao, tacos, tempura). If you prefer quiet conversation, aim for an earlier seating before the bar picks up.

reviews.text: Fantastic evening of food and drinks in a beautiful and immersively themed bar. Ken is a skilled bartender and was generous in sharing his insights while crafting delicious drinks. Food was fantastic. Other bartenders and hosts were warm and welcoming. The entire experience was great.

New Lucky find.  Loved this cool space and the food was very tasty  but the portions are small for the price.  We got 4 different  delicious dishes, terrific tempura cauliflower, duck tacos ( tiny) , short rib bao’s and 2 very small chicken skewers.  We liked it but we left a bit hungry.
Great drinks and hospitality! The bar team was amazing - Alex Alberto and Esteban!

The ambience is amazing, great for happy hour and catching up with friends but the food was NOT good. However, the staff was amazing and very accommodating, they took off all the items me and my party did not enjoy. I would go back but only for drinks
Unique place,  but food menu is still in progress.   Appetizers were pretty good.   Happy hour was a little confusing on mini drinks.   Nice decor though.

about:
Lucky's has been honoring the classic American steakhouse tradition since 2000. Founded in Montecito, California with a second location in Malibu, Lucky's opened it's first east coast location in Soho.

With 50 seats and a private dining room, Lucky's Soho brings the beloved brand to it's most intimate setting yet. The menu features classic Lucky's favorites such as ‘Gene’s Filet’ (filet mignon, fresh horseradish and red wine sauce), alongside NYC exclusives, such as thick-cut cajun bacon. A robust wine program and table side martini service round out the experience.

Lucky's is open for dinner every evening, lunch on Friday and brunch on Saturday and Sunday.

reviews.text: Amazing steak, went with friend John. Would come back 100%
Lucky to be visiting our son in NYC and he suggested dinner at Lucky’s (a month ago)!  Our meal was fantastic… service was attentive… ambience was cozy and inviting!  Memorable meal for sure!! 🥰

Great experience. Try the chicken! Highly recommended!

Not worth it. Food was expensive and average at best. Overly salty and nothing that left a lasting impression. It's also very loud as it is a very small space. Ambience was cool, I think people go here because it's "trendy" but there must be better steak houses in Soho.

about: Lume is a new Italian restaurant in the West Village that offers a unique dining experience. The restaurant is divided into two sections: a bar and a dining room. The bar is U-shaped and is adorned with a shower of lamps that give the space a chic and festive feel. The dining room features traditional French banquettes, beige tones, and bronze moldings for an ambiance of discreet luxury. The menu at Lume is a balance between French classics and Italian cuisine. There are two chefs in the kitchen, one Italian and one French. The menu features dishes such as arancinis with porcini mushrooms, grilled octopus, and wagyu beef carpaccio for starters. For main courses, there are comforting pasta dishes like ziti alla bolognese and bucatini cacio e pepe, as well as more adventurous options like scallops with rosemary and risotto with sun-dried tomatoes, or chicken parmesan with fontina cheese. The service at Lume is attentive, and the staff has been recruited from the owners' other two restaurants. The owners are a family business and are all very involved in the restaurant. They are lucky to have employees who have been loyal for years. Lume has been a success since it opened, and it continues to be popular with both

name: Ma-Dé
about:
Cédric and Ochi Vongerichten, the power couple behind the two popular NYC restaurants Wayan and Ma•dé, are thrilled to introduce a beloved form of dining from Indonesia to their second popular restaurant Ma•dé Padang style dining.

Originating in the coastal Indonesian province of West Sumatra, Padang style of dining is
omnipresent in cities across Indonesia and in neighboring countries such as Malaysia and
Singapore. Various dishes are served family-style all at once, often on a long table, to be shared
communally and eaten with the hands, although the use of a fork and spoon is acceptable as
well. Influenced by Indian and Middle Eastern cuisine, Padang dishes consist of three main
elements: gulai (curry), lado (chili pepper), and bareh (rice), and often uses coconut milk and
spicy chili, creating a symphony of bold flavors. All spreads contain a main protein, rice, and
accompanying vegetable and meat/egg/seafood dishes.
